concepts.def: Component sensing the environment or user (switch, sensor, microphone) and feeding a signal into an electronic system.
Component performing the system's logic, ranging from simple op-amps to microcontrollers like the Arduino Uno (released 2010).
Component producing the system's response, such as LED, motor, speaker or display.
Integrated circuit containing CPU, memory and I/O on a single chip, programmable for embedded control applications.
Component limiting current flow, with values typically marked by colour bands following the standard E12 or E24 series.
Digital building block performing Boolean operations such as AND, OR and NOT, fundamental to all digital electronics.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Electronic Systems & Programmable Components — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Electronic Systems & Programmable Components brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Electronic Systems & Programmable Components.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is a programmable single-chip computer for embedded use called?
options: Resistor
Microcontroller
Capacitor
Transistor

mcqs.q: In what year was the Arduino Uno released?
What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
Repair (because it sounds eco-friendly).
They are the same thing with different names.

mcqs.q: What does 'Rethink' mean in the 6 Rs?
options: Thinking about marketing the product.
Trying a design again if it does not work first time.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
Questioning whether a product is necessary or could be designed differently for sustainability.

mcqs.q: Which of the 6 Rs has the GREATEST environmental benefit?
options: Recycle (because it is most familiar).
Refuse or Reduce (preventing the impact at source).
Repair (because it sounds eco-friendly).
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
